edges.reason: Constructor assigns the name state variable.
Constructor assigns the symbol state variable.
Constructor assigns the decimals state variable.
Constructor sets _totalSupply to the initial minted amount.
Constructor writes the full supply into balances for the deployer.
Constructor mints the entire supply to msg.sender, so caller identity controls initial ownership.
approve writes allowance keyed by msg.sender, so caller identity governs authorization.
transfer debits balances[msg.sender], caller identity controls whose funds move.
transferFrom spends allowance of msg.sender, caller identity controls allowance deduction.
totalSupply() reads the _totalSupply state variable.
balances[address(0)] is read while computing an unchecked subtraction in totalSupply().
Unchecked _totalSupply - balances[address(0)] subtraction can underflow and corrupt the reported supply.
balanceOf reads the balances mapping.
allowance reads the allowed mapping.
approve writes into the allowed mapping.
spender parameter is used as the allowance key in approve.
transfer reads balances[msg.sender] as the left operand of the subtraction.
transfer reads balances[to] as the left operand of the addition.
transferFrom reads and writes balances[from] and balances[to] around the allowance subtraction.
transferFrom reads allowed[from][msg.sender] before decrementing it.
tokens parameter is subtracted from the sender balance; an oversized value would underflow without SafeMath.
tokens parameter is added to the recipient balance, an arithmetic-sensitive amount.
to parameter selects the recipient slot written by the addition.
from parameter selects the balance/allowance slots consumed by the subtraction.
tokens parameter is subtracted both from balances[from] and from the allowance.
transfer depends on safeSub for balance deduction, which reverts on underflow.
transfer depends on safeAdd for balance crediting, which reverts on overflow.
transferFrom depends on safeSub for balance and allowance deduction.
transferFrom depends on safeAdd for crediting the recipient.
Operand a flows into the arithmetic result in SafeMath functions.
Operand b flows into the arithmetic result in SafeMath functions.
Operand a flows into the subtraction in safeSub.
Operand b flows into the subtraction in safeSub.
safeAdd writes the local result variable c.
safeSub writes the local result variable c.
transfer returns the local success flag set to true.
approve returns the local success flag set to true.
transferFrom returns the local success flag set to true.

normalization_plan.reason: The tokens parameter only feeds the balance/allowance subtractions in transfer and transferFrom, so it is absorbed by the unsafe subtraction operation.
The to parameter only selects the recipient slot of the addition, so it is absorbed by the unsafe addition operation in transfer.
The from parameter only selects the source slots consumed by the allowance subtraction, so it is absorbed by that unsafe operation.
The spender parameter is only used as an allowance key inside approve, so it merges into the approve function.
Operand a is only consumed as arithmetic input inside the SafeMath functions, so it merges into safeAdd.
Operand b is only consumed as arithmetic input inside the SafeMath functions, so it merges into safeAdd.
Local result c is written and returned only within the SafeMath functions, so it merges into safeAdd.
Local success flag is set and returned only by the transfer-family functions, so it merges into transfer.
